label: The portraits on the equatorial armillary's pedestal
date: c. 1584 (instrument built) – December 1596 (the recording block's first issue); the inscribed '1580' is Tycho's floruit year, not an execution date
maker: Unrecorded. Christianson's 'probably painted by Gemperle' remains an uncited hedge (grade C) — Beckett & Christensen 1921 never mention these portraits, and DBL's Gemperlin entry is silent on the armillary. Gemperlin WAS available: recruited at Augsburg 1575, royal settlement letter 23 April 1577, documented in Denmark from 1578, died 1587 of a Copenhagen epidemic on Tycho's own printed testimony (De mundi II, p. 284) — his residency brackets the whole preferred painting window.

label: The Stjerneborg astronomer cycle — Tycho as the terminus of his own science
maker: Unrecorded. Tycho names nobody. Beckett & Christensen assume Tobias Gemperlin 'stiltiende' and attach the meteorological-diary painter entries of spring 1591 to this cycle — impossible, since Gemperlin was dead by 1587. No source documents any painter. Hans van Steenwinckel — documented at Stjerneborg's design and construction (c. 1584, resident on Hven through 1590) and as painter of the mural quadrant's perspectival architecture — is the best-profiled alternative, likewise unattested for this cycle. Christianson's Gemperle sentence restates Beckett (his entry cites Christensen & Beckett 1921, 18–21) and is not independent evidence.
city: Site only: Stjerneborg, island of Ven, Skåne, Sweden

label: The Frederiksborg oil (attributed to Gemperlin) — known through C. A. Jensen's 1838 copy
maker: Attributed to Tobias Gemperlin (Augsburg painter in Tycho's service from 1575, dead of the Copenhagen plague by 1587). The attribution is scholarly consensus resting on the working relationship, not on a signature or document — and the hedge is foundational, not late: Friis ('vel det sandsynligste, at det har været et Originalportræt, malet af Gemperlin') and Madsen ('vel') both hedged it at the outset, and Mortensen and the Dansk Biografisk Leksikon hedge it still. Beckett's 1897 case compared Jensen's copy only to the 1586 engraving and a sketch then under Goltzius's name — derivatives to derivatives, never to the signed Vedel 1578 or St Ibb 1578 anchors — and Karlson (1928), who also showed that Beckett attributed Gemperlin works from reproductions, doubted the attribution in a single unreasoned clause judged 'efter kopian'. Hans Knieper is excluded as a rival hand by Tycho's own division-of-labour statement on the 1587 mural quadrant.

label: The gilt portrait supralibros — two dies
maker: Cutter unrecorded. With the die now dated before late March 1588, Gemperlin (dead by 1587) is possible as designer and Hans Crol, Tycho's goldsmith on Hven (d. 30 November 1591), as cutter — but these are names of convenience, neither documented. The die pair's relationship is genuinely open: 1597 is the small die's first documented use, not a cutting date. If it is a later cutting it needs another hand; but Friis (c. 1890) held the small die the older of the pair — undefended, and the shared design cannot by itself discriminate one commission from two cuttings off one pattern.
holder: Best-documented example: Det Kongelige Bibliotek, Copenhagen
inventory: LN 432 2°, eks. 2 — Tycho's presentation copy of the Mechanica to Petr Vok z Rožmberka

label: De Gheyn's first engraving (Westergaard 1377) — the 'overloaded' portrait
maker: Jacques de Gheyn II (Antwerp 1565 – The Hague 1629), signed in the plate; an independent Amsterdam engraver by 1588, previously trained in Goltzius's Haarlem workshop. No document names Goltzius anywhere in the commission — the old account that the commission 'went to Goltzius, who passed it to his pupil' is Beckett & Christensen's 1921 conjecture, built on premises (a dependent pupil; engravings of 1586) that are both refuted.

inventory: KKS4530 (state I, no address); KKSgb7575 (state II, 'Marco Sadeler excudit')

label: The Copenhagen pen drawing (SMK KKSgb5254) — the second engraving's production drawing
maker: Jacques de Gheyn II is the best-supported hand (the pen medium is his documented practice for portrait-print models — 'Goltzius never did' so, per Reznicek — and the sheet's idiom matches his secure Marnix model); a residual alternative is an unidentified copyist supplying the model. Tobias Gemperlin is excluded as draughtsman (dead by 1587, and no secure Gemperlin drawing exists to compare). The old Goltzius attribution is refuted for authorship (no Tycho in Reznicek's corpus, wrong medium, Goltzius in Italy from late 1590); its documentary trail is a pre-1890s common opinion — still the museum's displayed label in 1921 — revived by Mortensen 1946 on the strength of a verso mark first recorded that year (Mortensen: the name Goltzius; Altena/SMK: a red-chalk 'HG' monogram) and judged forged by both the museum and the de Gheyn catalogue.
holder: Statens Museum for Kunst, Den Kongelige Kobberstiksamling
